Concept: a cathedral-vault ooze that digests reliquaries
Challenge Rating: 9

THE SHELF (id — what it plays like — printed exemplars):
- brute — a plain bruiser — big weapon or big limbs, stands and trades, no trick (Ogre, Hill Giant, Minotaur)
- brute-charger — runs prey down — a straight rush that hits hardest at the end, gores, tramples the prone (Gorgon, Rhinoceros, Triceratops)
- brute-grappler — a solid BODY that seizes and holds — jaws, coils, tentacles, a maw or cage that swallows, engulfs, smothers, or drags prey inside itself (a ghost that pulls you under is lurker-phantom) (Roper, Giant Constrictor Snake, Otyugh, Purple Worm)
- brute-juggernaut — a MADE thing — poured, forged, carved, or animated stone or metal; immune to being reshaped, breaks what it walks through (Stone Golem, Iron Golem, Animated Armor (large))
- brute-regenerator — its wounds close as fast as they open — flesh, wax, or iron that reknits, regrows, or reassembles; only its bane stops it (Troll, Hydra)
- skirmisher — a mobile hit-and-run attacker — pack tactics, dart in, dart out (Wolf, Gnoll, Hobgoblin)
- skirmisher-mounted — a RIDER, or a beast carrying one — speed, momentum, ride-down attacks that carry it past the target; a lone charging beast with no rider is brute-charger (Knight on a warhorse, Centaur, Wight cavalry)
- skirmisher-skulker — a bodied sneak — hides, strikes with advantage, vanishes; a living or solid creature, never a ghost (Assassin, Doppelganger, Goblin Boss)
- skirmisher-hurler — a thrower — boulders, spears, nets, javelins, reeling lines; a physical creature that fights at range with its arm (Hill Giant (rocks), Cyclops, a net-thrower)
- skirmisher-archer — a SHOOTER — bows, crossbows, slings, darts; a creature whose primary attack is a missile it does not throw, and who keeps its distance (Scout, Spy, a kobold sniper, a hobgoblin longbow line)
- skirmisher-shifter — a creature of TWO FORMS — a humanoid that becomes a beast or a hybrid, or a thing that wears other shapes; some attacks belong to one form only (Werewolf, Weretiger, Doppelganger)
- skirmisher-winged — a flyer — dives, swooping strikes, snatches and drops, attacks on the wing (Griffon, Wyvern, Peryton)
- lurker — a stalker — invisible or hidden, one devastating opening strike, then the hide-cycle (Invisible Stalker, Hunter Shark, Displacer Beast)
- lurker-phantom — an incorporeal dead or spectral thing — drifts through walls, drains the living, cannot bear the light; a ghost or spirit is ALWAYS this (Ghost, Wraith, Specter, Shadow)
- lurker-trap — it IS the ambush — a disguised, rooted, or attached thing that looks harmless or holds still until prey is close, then springs (Mimic, Piercer, Gargoyle (perched), Trapper)
- caster — fragile ranged magic — bolts, blasts, a spell list, keeps its distance (Mage, Archmage, Flameskull)
- caster-binder — a hexer — curses, rays, and conditions over raw damage; wins by taking enemies' actions away, not their Hit Points (Green Hag, Night Hag, a witch or warlock)
- caster-warpriest — an armored battle-cleric or crusader — weapon strikes that carry holy or profane energy, prayers as war-gear (Priest, War Priest, a paladin-shaped fiend)
- defender — a living soldier or bodyguard — shield, armor, holds the line, punishes anyone who moves past (Knight, Guard Captain, Veteran)
- defender-leader — a COMMANDER whose signature is what it does for allies — an aura of authority, a parry, a captain who fights beside troops; a warlord, chieftain, captain, sergeant (Hobgoblin Captain, Bandit Captain, Pirate Captain)
- defender-warden — a MADE or risen guardian bound to a charge — a construct sentinel or tomb-bound spirit that shields something specific with its own body (Shield Guardian, Helmed Horror, a tomb golem)
- swarm — a mass of small creatures (or small things) acting as one — occupies space, halves when bloodied (Swarm of Insects, Swarm of Bats, Swarm of Ravens)
- ooze — an amorphous body — no fixed shape, corrodes or engulfs, squeezes through cracks; the body IS the ooze, not a coating or a mouthful (Black Pudding, Gelatinous Cube, Ochre Jelly)
- dragon — a true dragon — breath weapon, flight, frightful presence, the whole kit in one body (Adult Red Dragon, Young Green Dragon, Wyrmling)

- A CUE YOU CONFIRM IS A PICK YOU MAKE. If you answer "means": true for a key word above, that key's chassis MUST appear among your picks. Confirming a cue and then ranking a different chassis is one answer contradicting itself; decide which it is and answer both fields the same way.
- Rank up to THREE picks, best first. For EACH pick, quote the phrase of the concept that earns it ("because") — copy the words as written. A pick you cannot quote for is a pick you should not make: the engine checks every quote against the input and discards picks it cannot find there.
- What the creature IS outranks what it DOES to its victims, and what it uses, hunts, wears, rides, or is compared to. An incorporeal or drowned dead thing that pulls, drags, or drowns the living is lurker-phantom, never brute-grappler: the grappler is a BODY that holds prey in its grip or inside itself. A troll-hunter is not a troll; a knight who rides a horse is mounted but not a beast; a sword forged by a golem is not a golem; a thing with a tar-slick mouth is not an ooze.
- brute-juggernaut and defender-warden are MADE or risen things (construct, elemental, undead, plant, ooze). Living flesh, however armored, takes another chassis.
- swarm, ooze, and dragon only when the BODY is that thing — a mass of many, an amorphous mass, a true dragon. lurker-phantom too: only when the body is INCORPOREAL. The drowned, the buried and the hanged are usually corpses that walk, and a corpse that drags people down by the ankles has hands and weight — pick it a body that can hold someone. A phantom drifts through a wall and cannot.
- A concept that holds, seizes, swallows, entombs, or folds shut around prey is brute-grappler however it is built — that chassis alone carries the containment engine. A thing that traps by LOOKING harmless is lurker-trap.
- creature_type from the concept's SUBSTANCE — what it physically is: animated objects and machines are Construct; remains or spirits of the dead are Undead; natural animals are Beast; fungus and vegetation are Plant; giants are Giant. Humanoid is the NPC type — a remade, fused, grown, or woven thing is a Monstrosity however upright it stands. Never type by vibe.

    swallow — swallows a creature whole and holds it inside
    gaze — a look that afflicts whoever meets or sees it
    snare — traps or roots a creature in place where it stands
    grapple — seizes and holds a creature, or hauls it along
    shove — pushes, pulls or knocks a creature off its feet
    charm — compels, lures, taunts or calms — it chooses for them
    fear — frightens: the target flees or cannot face it
    dazzle — blinds, deafens, stuns or marks a target's senses
    charge — runs or leaps at them, trampling through or landing on
    breath — exhales something over an area — fire, gas, spores, cold
    burst — an explosion, a hurled thing, or a blast on its death
    drain — takes life, strength or hit points out of a creature
    curse — a lasting affliction, disease, brand or debt it lays on one target
    retaliate — something happens to whoever hits, touches or grabs it
    climb — goes where others cannot — walls, webs, earth, rough ground
    teleport — blinks, phases or vanishes from where it stood
    zone — the ground or air around it is harmful or hard to cross
    disguise — passes for something else, or is hard to make out
    harden — turns aside blows — a shell, a stance, a sealed body
    resist — shrugs off or absorbs a kind of harm entirely
    escalate — GROWS STRONGER AS THE FIGHT TURNS: harder when wounded, when enraged, when it has already felled someone, or AGAINST A TARGET THAT IS ALREADY AFFLICTED (a blow that finds the frightened, the prone, the poisoned)
    mend — heals or repairs itself or an ally
    command — orders, rallies or buffs its allies
    track — always knows where a creature is, or never loses it
    harvest — what it kills stays dead, or cannot be raised
    relic — an object it carries or guards that its power runs through

WHAT ELSE DO THE WORDS NAME? Three more, each with the user's own words quoted in "because" (leave a field out if the words do not settle it):
- "shoots": true only when this creature's own attack is a BOW, CROSSBOW, SLING or a thrown shot at range — a sniper, an archer. False for one that merely watches from a distance, and false when its ranged power is magic or a breath.
- "is_a_swarm": true only when the creature IS a mass of many small things acting as one body. False for a creature that COMMANDS or is accompanied by animals, and false for one that merely resembles a crowd.
- "swarm_of": ONLY when is_a_swarm is true — the plural noun for the many small things, as a GM would read it on the card: "funeral bells", "rats", "stinging flies". Print names every swarm "Swarm of <this>". Omit it otherwise.
- "hold_shape": HOW this creature takes hold of a creature, if it does. One of five words.
  "grip" — jaws, claws, a grab that needs it right beside its target: a hound, a crocodile, a bear, an ogre. Print writes 48 of these. A hound that "drags fishermen under" is GRIP: the drag IS its bite, and it has nothing to pull a creature in with from twenty feet away.
  "reach" — a part that goes OUT and hauls the target back: a tentacle, a tongue, a lash, a chain, a harpoon line, a web it reels in. Print writes four — the Roper (60 feet), the Kraken (30), the Aboleth and the Tarrasque (15).

  "medium" — it commands mud, water, vines or sand it is NOT made of, and that closes over the target. Print has none of these.
  "none" — it does not take hold of creatures at all.
  Judge the CREATURE, not its mood or its job. "because" quotes the GM's own words for any answer but "none".

("casts") True when the words name magic outright ("casts", "spells", "hexes") and ALSO when the KIND implies it: a cleric, a crusader who smites, a chaplain who blesses, a druid, a warlock. False for a plain warrior however armoured, false for a title alone, and false for a creature whose uncanny power is its BODY rather than a worked art — a fey piper's music, a gaze, a breath weapon. Write the synthesis so that material is visible in what it is and what it does.

Deterministic checks (math, DCs, damage bands, known formatting rules) have
already run — do NOT re-check arithmetic, CR calibration, or damage budgets.
Your job is the judgment layer: defects of adjudicability, counterplay, and
internal consistency that pattern-matching cannot catch.

A defect is anything that would cost a GM or a player at the table: an effect
that cannot be adjudicated, a state with no rules-legal response — and equally a
row that is not worth its action, cannot be run in the time a turn allows, or does
not make practical sense for the creature it is on. A row can be perfectly correct
and still be a defect, because a GM who cannot use it got nothing.



WHERE THESE ROWS CAME FROM — this changes what a finding on each is worth:
- THE BODY'S OWN ROW — ours, from the donor catalog: Traits/Amorphous, Traits/Corrosive Form, Traits/Spider Climb, Actions/Multiattack, Actions/Engulfing Pseudopod

  rows against, and they are NOT under review. Do not flag their wording, their phrasing, their
  RULES, their counterplay, a missing escape DC or duration or limit, how long they take to resolve,

  written — you are not auditing the Monster Manual, and a published row is what a good row looks
  like.

  a published row, and it is the most valuable finding you can make.
- THE BODY'S rows are ours, shared with every creature built on this body.

1. COUNTERPLAY. Every imposed state has a rules-legal path out, written in the

   another space). Frequency gates (1/Day, Recharge, "only while Bloodied") do

   agency once affected. An attack-roll-only effect that removes a creature
   from play with no save and no escape is a defect regardless of gating.

2. ADJUDICABILITY. Every effect answers: when does it happen (trigger, timing,
   or action cost), where does it apply (area, range, or target), and when does
   it end (duration or end condition). An aura with no area, a save effect with
   no range, a trait that describes an activity with no action cost, a
   condition with no duration — each is a defect. Also flag any effect whose
   resolution requires information the block does not provide (a referenced
   zone, object, or state that nothing defines or creates — e.g. spores that
   are never applied, a minion that is never created, "its arrival point" with

   always a defect.

3. SELF-CONSISTENCY. Entries must not contradict the block or themselves:
   abilities keyed to movement modes the creature lacks, conditions applied to
   targets immune to them by the block's own rider (e.g. Poisoned applied by a

   defect needed. Also flag 2014-format save phrasing ("must succeed on a DC X ... saving throw or").

sheet.name: Reliquary Ooze
sheet.senses: blindsight 60 ft. (blind beyond this radius), passive Perception 9

abilities.name: Wounded Hunger
abilities.description: The ooze has advantage on attack rolls against any creature that doesn't have all its hit points. The ooze can pinpoint the location of consecrated relics within 60 feet of itself.

abilities.name: Amorphous
abilities.description: The ooze can move through a space as narrow as 1 inch wide without squeezing.

abilities.name: Corrosive Form
abilities.description: A creature that touches the ooze or hits it with a melee attack while within 5 feet of it takes 9 (2d8) acid damage.

abilities.name: Spider Climb
abilities.description: The ooze can climb difficult surfaces, including along ceilings, without needing to make an ability check.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The ooze makes two Engulfing Pseudopod attacks.

actions.name: Engulfing Pseudopod
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +7 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 16 (3d8 + 3) bludgeoning damage plus 11 (2d10) acid damage.

actions.name: Reliquary Spray (Recharge 5-6)
actions.description: Each creature in a 30-foot-long, 5-foot-wide line must make a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw, taking 38 (11d6) acid damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. On a failed save, the target is also blinded until the end of its next turn.
